Hmm, the failing CIs consistently fail in "boot-services". I need to figure out what this means. It seems CentosCI is now fixed.

I figured out the cause of the failure in ubuntuautopkgtests:
when fexecve is used, /proc/pid/status shows `Name: 3`, which means that `ps -C foobar` doesn't work. `pidof` works, because it checks `/proc/self/cmdline`. `/proc/self/exe` also shows the correct link, but requires privileges to read. `/proc/self/comm` also shows "3".

I'll file a PR for the debian packaging to use pidof.

The question is: do we consider the comm/status ugliness a deal-breaker? Do we consider it enough of a deal-breaker to make the fexecve() thing opt-in at compile time?
Updated with the one tiny fix (s/1/EXIT_FAILURE/) and one additional commit to make fexecve/execveat use a compile time option. PTAL.

review_comments: this is a bummer of course. i wished it would just work.
wasn't sizeof() of VLA particularly ugly, because needs eval at runtime? wasn't that something to avoid? i don#t remember the details, but i thought there was somehting

I tried to check this. VLA allocation is indeed quite expensive, approx. 60 instructions in unoptimized mode. But with `a[n + 1]` there isn't much difference between `ELEMENTSOF(a)` and just `n + 1`. In both in unoptimized mode gcc does some calculation and pushes to the right register. (There is shl and shr with ELEMENTSOF, which is probably more expensive than the add which is done in the other case, but I don't think we need to go into this level of microoptimization.)

With optimization though, gcc replaces the VLA with a simple %rsp adjustment and the ELEMENTSOF with a single move. So I think there is no need to change the code.
